knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Visible cleanliness shows housekeeping, not decontamination or biological clearance. Verification belongs to the laboratory owner and qualified testers.
The cleaner refuses the certification, records the housekeeping done and refers verification to the laboratory owner. A disclaimer does not make an unsupported certificate acceptable.
The handover lists the housekeeping done, what was not touched and every exclusion. It does not state sterility or safety.
A visual check cannot test for absence of biological material, so the line is marked not tested and referred to the owner. A tick would record a result that was never obtained.

practicalCriteria: Writes a housekeeping-only handover for a fictional laboratory zone that lists the tidied areas, untouched areas and every exclusion.
Refuses a simulated certification request for biological safety, and refers the verification to the laboratory owner in writing.
Marks a fictional inspection criterion that the visual check cannot test as not tested, rather than ticking it.
Records the simulated deferral with the return criteria and the responsible contact.
passRule: Handover housekeeping-only with exclusions, certification refused and referred, untested criteria not ticked, and deferral recorded with return criteria. Observed by an assessor in a supervised desk exercise. Not a clearance, and a knowledge check result alone is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Refusal and referral record, with the return criteria
Fictional inspection sheet showing untested criteria marked as not tested
stopWorkCriteria: Certification signed for laboratory biological safety
Sterility, decontamination or clearance claimed in the handover or the record
Inspection criterion ticked without a test that supports it
Handover issued without the exclusions listed
